prompt.context_jp: 慌ただしい一日の疲れで、頭の中___まだ会社のことでいっぱいだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭の中___まだ会社のことでいっぱいだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (Hotaru reflecting after a hectic day.)

feedback.correct_en: は marks 頭の中 as the topic being described — 'as for my head, it was still full of work thoughts.' This is reflective framing, not new information.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 頭の中 as newly spotlighted information, which doesn't fit this introspective continuation. を doesn't work with the stative いっぱいだった.

contrast_examples.jp: 頭の中はパニックだった。
contrast_examples.en: My head was in a panic. (describing an ongoing state)

contrast_examples.jp: 急に頭の中が真っ白になった。
contrast_examples.en: Suddenly my mind went blank. (new event — が)

prompt.context_jp: ビールの泡___とうに消え、ぬるくなった液体が月明かりを映している。
prompt.prompt_jp: ビールの泡___とうに消え…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits best here?

feedback.correct_en: は sets ビールの泡 as the topic being commented on, then contrasts with the second clause about the liquid (液体が). This は/が pairing creates the contrast between foam and liquid.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the foam as newly introduced information. Here the foam is set up as a topic, and the new/descriptive information falls on 液体が in the next clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 泡は消えたが、液体は残った。
contrast_examples.en: The foam disappeared, but the liquid remained. (topic contrast)
Oh, the foam disappeared! (noticing — new info)

prompt.context_jp: トラブルの後始末にかけては、社内で高野の右に出る者___いないと言われていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高野の右に出る者___いない
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: In existence statements (〜がいない) describing 'there is no one who...', が marks the existing/non-existing subject. This is the standard pattern for 右に出る者がいない.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize 'the person who surpasses him' as if already known — unnatural here where the claim is that such a person doesn't exist at all.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼に勝てる者がいない。
contrast_examples.en: There is no one who can beat him.

contrast_examples.jp: その人は会社にいない。
contrast_examples.en: That person isn't at the company. (specific known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 親指___発信ボタンの上で一瞬ためらい、それから静かに押し込まれた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 親指___発信ボタンの上で一瞬ためらい…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (Narrative description of Takano's thumb.)

feedback.correct_en: が introduces 親指 as the narrative's new focal subject — the camera zooms in on the thumb performing the action. This is classic descriptive narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'thumb' a familiar topic, which feels off in cinematic description where the thumb is freshly spotlighted.

contrast_examples.en: A tear ran down her cheek. (narrative description — が)
That finger was slender. (commenting on a known topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 一生懸命 恋愛して来た人の所に___… 恋の神様みたいな そういうのが ついてるんじゃないかって思うんです｡
prompt.prompt_jp: 恋愛して来た人の所に___…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (Hotaru explaining her 'God of Love' theory.)

feedback.correct_en: に+は marks the location as a contrastive topic: 'as for those who've worked hard at love, something like a God of Love is attached to them.' The contrast is with people like herself (next sentence).
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot follow に to mark the location. で would suggest 'at that place' as a means/setting, not the possessor-location sense the sentence needs.

contrast_examples.jp: 努力した人には運がついてくる。
contrast_examples.en: Luck follows those who work hard. (contrastive topic location)

contrast_examples.jp: 私のところには来てくれない。
contrast_examples.en: It won't come to someone like me. (contrasting with others)

prompt.context_jp: 久しぶりに 恋___落ちたんだろう？
prompt.prompt_jp: 久しぶりに 恋___落ちた
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in 恋___落ちる?

feedback.correct_en: 恋に落ちる is the fixed collocation meaning 'to fall in love.' に marks the endpoint of 'falling into.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 恋を落ちる is ungrammatical; 恋で落ちる would mean 'to fail because of love,' not 'to fall in love.'

contrast_examples.en: I fell in love at first sight.
To fall into a hole. (same に endpoint pattern)

prompt.context_jp: 思い___ 言葉にしなければ 伝わらないんだよ｡
prompt.prompt_jp: 思い___ 言葉にしなければ 伝わらない
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (Takano's advice to Hotaru.)

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 思い as a generic truth: 'as for feelings, they don't get across unless put into words.' This is a maxim-like statement.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like one specific feeling is suddenly at issue. を doesn't fit with the intransitive 伝わる.

contrast_examples.jp: 愛は言葉にしないと伝わらない。
contrast_examples.en: Love doesn't come across unless spoken. (generic truth — は)
That feeling got across. (specific instance — が)

prompt.context_jp: 心臓の音___、自分の耳にまで聞こえてくるほどうるさかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 心臓の音___、自分の耳にまで聞こえてくるほど…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this narrative moment?

feedback.correct_en: が marks 心臓の音 as a newly spotlighted sensation at this tense moment — Hotaru suddenly notices how loud her heartbeat is. This is new information surging into awareness.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the heartbeat as an already-established topic, losing the sense of sudden noticing that drives this scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に鼓動が速くなった。
contrast_examples.en: My pulse suddenly quickened. (new sensation — が)
My heart is strong. (general topic description — は)

prompt.context_jp: 会議室の時計の秒針だけ___、やけに大きな音を刻んでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の秒針だけ___、やけに大きな音を刻んでいた
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after だけ here?

feedback.correct_en: だけが gives exhaustive focus — 'only the second hand (and nothing else) was ticking loudly.' This matches the atmosphere of silence broken by one sound.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would mean 'at least the second hand' (contrastive 'at least'), which weakens the exhaustive effect. を doesn't fit this subject slot.

contrast_examples.en: Only you are my support. (exhaustive focus — が)
At least this I won't yield on. (contrastive — は)

prompt.context_jp: 友達でいると決めたのだから、普通にしていればいいのだと自分___言い聞かせる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分___言い聞かせる
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 言い聞かせる?

feedback.correct_en: 言い聞かせる takes に to mark the addressee: '自分に言い聞かせる' means to tell/convince oneself. The recipient of the telling is marked with に.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would wrongly make 自分 the object of the verb. で would indicate means, not the person being addressed.

contrast_examples.en: To admonish a child. (に = addressee)
To ask oneself. (same に pattern)

prompt.context_jp: ポケットから携帯電話___取り出し、履歴に並んだ同じ番号をしばらく見つめた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ポケットから携帯電話___取り出し…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the object?

feedback.correct_en: を marks 携帯電話 as the direct object of 取り出す (take out). The source (ポケットから) is already marked with から.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the phone a subject, not the thing being taken. に would indicate a destination, which doesn't fit 取り出す.

contrast_examples.en: Take a book out of the bag.
Take money out of a wallet.

prompt.context_jp: いつも厳しく、隙のない上司___、あんなふうに自分のことを語るのを初めて聞いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隙のない上司___、あんなふうに自分のことを語るのを初めて聞いた
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (Hotaru reflecting on Takano.)

feedback.correct_en: が marks 上司 as the subject of the embedded clause (上司が...語るのを聞いた). Inside a subordinate clause whose head is the nominalized のを, the subject typically takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は is generally avoided inside relative/nominalized clauses that aren't the main predicate; it would create a jarring topic break within the embedded structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生が歌うのを聞いた。
contrast_examples.en: I heard the teacher sing. (embedded subject — が)
That teacher is interesting. (main-clause topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: しばらく遠ざかっていた 私の所に___ 恋の神様は 来てくれないのかも…
prompt.prompt_jp: 私の所に___ 恋の神様は 来てくれないのかも
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (Contrasting herself with people who work at love.)

feedback.correct_en: には sets 私の所 in contrast to '恋愛してきた人の所' from the previous line — 'but to someone like me, the God of Love probably won't come.' This is textbook contrastive は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot follow に to mark a location in this pattern. も ('also') would reverse the meaning, suggesting the god does come to her too.

contrast_examples.jp: 他の人には来ても、私には来ない。
contrast_examples.en: Even if it comes to others, it won't come to me. (contrast)

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の家には明かりがついている。
contrast_examples.en: The light is on at his house. (topic location)

prompt.context_jp: 私に___ やっぱり うまく行かない恋愛より うまく行く友達関係のほうが いいんです｡
prompt.prompt_jp: 私に___ やっぱり…友達関係のほうがいいんです
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: には contrasts her preference with others' — 'for me (as opposed to other people), friendship is better than a failing romance.' The contrastive/topic は is standard with the '〜には〜のほうがいい' pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot follow に to mark a person's standpoint. を doesn't fit this evaluative pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 私にはこっちのほうが合ってる。
contrast_examples.en: For me, this one suits better.
What would be good for you?

prompt.context_jp: 背中越しに感じる手嶋の沈黙___、かえって彼女を追い立てる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 手嶋の沈黙___、かえって彼女を追い立てる
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: が marks 沈黙 as the agent newly driving the action — the silence itself is what propels her. It introduces a specific force acting in this moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize 'silence' as if already a known theme, dampening the dramatic effect of the silence suddenly pushing her forward.

contrast_examples.en: His silence was scary. (specific force — が)
Silence is golden. (generic topic — は)

prompt.context_jp: 蛍はその隣___腰を下ろし、しばらく黙って夜風に吹かれていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: その隣___腰を下ろし
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 腰を下ろす?

feedback.correct_en: に marks the endpoint of the action of sitting down — the location one settles into. 腰を下ろす takes に for where you end up.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks where an ongoing action happens, not the destination of a settling motion. を doesn't fit a location here.

contrast_examples.en: Sit down on a bench.
Play in the park. (ongoing action — で)

prompt.context_jp: 不思議なことに、胸の中___泣く前よりもずっと軽くなっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 胸の中___泣く前よりもずっと軽くなっていた
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 胸の中 for reflective comment: 'as for her chest/heart, it felt much lighter than before crying.' The comparison (〜よりも) also aligns with topic framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the chest as a new participant surging into focus, which doesn't match this calm, reflective tone.

contrast_examples.en: My heart felt clear. (introspective topic — は)
Suddenly my chest hurt. (new sensation — が)

prompt.context_jp: その気持を ___ と思え｡
prompt.prompt_jp: その気持を ___ と思え
prompt.prompt_en: Takano tells Hotaru to cherish her feelings. Which word fits?

feedback.correct_en: いとおしい means 'precious, dear, something to cherish.' Takano is urging Hotaru to treasure the fact that she can love again.
feedback.incorrect_en: やかましい means 'noisy/annoying,' and わずらわしい means 'troublesome' — both are negative and reverse Takano's intended message.

contrast_examples.en: A precious memory.
Troublesome relationships.

prompt.context_jp: このたびは 誠に ___ でした｡
prompt.prompt_jp: このたびは 誠に ___ でした
prompt.prompt_en: Takano is apologizing to a client. Which phrase fits?

feedback.correct_en: 申し訳ございませんでした is the standard business-apology formula paired with このたびは 誠に. It matches the formal, client-facing tone of Takano's call.
feedback.incorrect_en: ごめんなさい is casual/personal; すまなかった is blunt/masculine — neither fits a formal apology to a client on the phone.

contrast_examples.jp: このたびは誠に申し訳ございませんでした。
contrast_examples.en: We are truly sorry for what happened this time. (business)
Sorry I'm late. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: トラブルの後始末にかけては、社内で高野の ___ 者はいないと言われていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 高野の ___ 者はいない
prompt.prompt_en: Which idiom means 'no one surpasses Takano'?

feedback.correct_en: 右に出る者がいない is a set idiom meaning 'there's no one who can surpass (him)' — the seat on the right was historically the place of honor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目に入る means 'to come into sight'; 手が届く means 'to be within reach' — neither expresses superiority.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の右に出る者はいない。
contrast_examples.en: No one surpasses him.
It caught my eye.

prompt.context_jp: ハッハ～ン ___ で茶沸かすわ｡
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ で茶沸かすわ
prompt.prompt_en: Which body part completes this idiom meaning 'ridiculous/laughable'?

feedback.correct_en: へそで茶を沸かす literally 'boil tea with one's navel' is a set idiom meaning something is utterly absurd or laughable. Takano uses it to mock Hotaru's claim.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other body parts don't form this idiom — only へそ is used in this fixed expression of ridicule.

contrast_examples.en: That's a laughable story.
To sneer at (different idiom).

prompt.context_jp: 一体 君は 何時間 私を独りぼっちにさせれば ___ んだ！
prompt.prompt_jp: 何時間…させれば ___ んだ
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'be satisfied'?

feedback.correct_en: 気が済む means 'to feel satisfied/content'. Takano is angrily asking how many hours Hotaru needs to leave him alone before she'll be satisfied.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気が利く means 'to be considerate/thoughtful'; 気がする means 'to have a feeling that...' — neither fits this exasperated complaint.

contrast_examples.jp: 謝るまで気が済まない。
contrast_examples.en: I won't be satisfied until you apologize.
That person is considerate.

prompt.context_jp: ___ な思い出として 深い傷になる｡
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ な思い出として 深い傷になる
prompt.prompt_en: Takano fears the memory would be what kind?

feedback.correct_en: ぶざま means 'unsightly, pathetic, humiliating' — fitting Takano's fear of a humiliating memory becoming a deep wound after being rejected.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見事 ('splendid') and 鮮やか ('vivid/brilliant') are positive — they contradict the painful context.

contrast_examples.en: A humiliating failure.
A splendid victory.

prompt.context_jp: 真っ赤になっているであろう自分の顔は、___ ものに違いない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の顔は、___ ものに違いない
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'unbearable to look at'?

feedback.correct_en: 目も当てられない is a set phrase meaning 'can't bear to look at; too dreadful to see.' It perfectly captures Hotaru's embarrassment about her red face.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目にかける means 'to take care of/favor'; 目が利かない means 'to have poor judgment of quality' — neither fits.

contrast_examples.jp: 目も当てられない惨状。
contrast_examples.en: A scene too awful to look at.
To look after a junior.

prompt.context_jp: ようやく ___ がつき、蛍は空になったファイルを手に立ち上がった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ようやく ___ がつき
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'a stopping point/pause in work'?

feedback.correct_en: 区切りがつく means 'to reach a stopping point/milestone in a task.' It's the standard collocation for finishing a stage of work.
feedback.incorrect_en: 仕切り means 'partition/arrangement'; 手切り isn't a standard word. Only 区切り collocates with つく in this sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事に区切りがついた。
contrast_examples.en: I reached a stopping point in my work.

contrast_examples.jp: 部屋に仕切りをつける。
contrast_examples.en: Put a partition in the room.

prompt.context_jp: Takano's advice to Hotaru about speaking her feelings.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as Takano's heartfelt advice?

choices.text: 思いは 言葉にしなければ 伝わらないんだよ｡
思いは 言葉を しなければ 伝わらないんだよ｡
思いは 言葉で しなければ 伝わらないんだよ｡

feedback.correct_en: 言葉にする ('put into words') is the fixed collocation. The に marks the resulting form. This matches the original line and sounds natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言葉をする isn't an idiomatic expression. 言葉でする would mean 'do it using words' as a means, which doesn't convey 'put into words.'

contrast_examples.en: Put feelings into words.
Give shape to a dream. (same 〜にする pattern)

prompt.context_jp: Hotaru's confession to Teshima.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is the natural way to confess 'I like you'?

choices.text: あなたのことが好きです！
あなたのことを好きです！
あなたのことに好きです！

feedback.correct_en: 好きだ takes が to mark the thing liked — 'あなたのことが好き' is the natural confession pattern. 好き is a na-adjective, not a verb, so its target takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is for direct objects of verbs; 好き isn't a verb. に doesn't fit this adjectival-like predicate either.

contrast_examples.en: I like cats.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたのことが大好きです。
contrast_examples.en: I really like you.

prompt.context_jp: Describing someone unreachable despite many attempts.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural?

choices.text: 何度かけてもつながらなかった相手だった。
何度もかけたがつながれなかった相手だった。
つながらない何度もかけた相手だった。

feedback.correct_en: 何度かけても〜ない ('no matter how many times I called, it didn't connect') is a natural concessive pattern, and つながる (intransitive) is the correct verb for a call connecting.
feedback.incorrect_en: つながれる as a potential of つながる is awkward here; option c scrambles the modifier order unnaturally.

contrast_examples.jp: 何度言っても聞かない。
contrast_examples.en: No matter how often I say it, he won't listen.
The call won't connect.

prompt.context_jp: Takano telling Hotaru she can rest.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural as a boss's casual-but-firm dismissal at home?

choices.text: 君も もう休んでいいぞ｡
君も もう休んでいいです｡
君も もう休むがいい｡

feedback.correct_en: 〜ていいぞ with the masculine sentence-final ぞ fits Takano's authoritative but informal register when speaking to his subordinate at home. It matches the drama's original line.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ていいです sounds oddly polite coming from a boss to his junior; 休むがいい is an archaic/literary command that doesn't fit this intimate home scene.

contrast_examples.en: You can head home now. (boss, informal)

contrast_examples.jp: もう帰っていいですよ。
contrast_examples.en: You may go home now. (polite — e.g., to a customer)

prompt.context_jp: Takano telling Hotaru to cherish herself for being able to love again.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sentence is the most natural rendering?

choices.text: 久しぶりに 人を好きになることが できた自分を いとおしいと思いなさい｡
久しぶりに 人を好きになることを できた自分が いとおしいと思いなさい｡
久しぶりに 人が好きになることを できた自分に いとおしいと思いなさい｡

feedback.correct_en: 〜ことができる takes が to mark the ability's object, and いとおしいと思う takes を for the thing cherished. The original flows: 'cherish yourself (を) who was able to love (ことができた).'
feedback.incorrect_en: Swapping が and を breaks both collocations — ことができる requires が, and いとおしいと思う requires を for its object.

contrast_examples.en: I was able to speak. (ことが できる)

contrast_examples.jp: 自分をいとおしく思う。
contrast_examples.en: To cherish oneself.
